about: The long conversation (PLAN.md, part 2): 16 linked questions on one library paper no earlier test asked about, written by Claude from its pdftotext (experiments/big-library/text/cheme3/adsorption-2.txt) before any answer. `chat` is asked in a row in one conversation and may lean on earlier turns; `solo` is the same question spelled out, asked alone. Keys are the paper's printed values.

questions.chat: I'm reading the RSC Advances paper on how biochar loading affects pore accessibility and CO2 adsorption in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids. Which of its compositions gave the highest equilibrium CO2 uptake at 298 K and about 1 bar, and how much did it adsorb?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, which composition gave the highest equilibrium CO2 uptake at 298 K and about 1 bar, and how much did it adsorb?

questions.chat: How much activated biochar went into that composition's synthesis, and how much into the composition with twice its nominal loading?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, what mass of activated bamboo-derived biochar (A-BC) was used to make BC-10, and what mass for BC-20?
questions.expect: BC-10 37.1 mg, BC-20 83.5 mg of A-BC (sec. 2.2.2)
questions.trap: the precursor masses 0.230 g Al(NO3)3·9H2O or 0.104 g Me3BTC

questions.chat: Using the masses of the aluminium nitrate and Me3BTC precursors as well, check the nominal biochar loading of the best composition: what percentage do you get?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, compute BC-10's nominal biochar loading from the masses of A-BC, Al(NO3)3·9H2O and Me3BTC used in its synthesis. What percentage do you get?
questions.trap: the mmol amounts (0.613, 0.413) used as masses, or 37.1 / 230

questions.chat: At what temperature and for how long was the autoclave held during that synthesis?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, at what temperature and for how long was the Teflon-lined autoclave held in the solvothermal synthesis of the hybrids?
questions.trap: the biochar activation's 600 °C for 2 h, drying at 150 °C for 12 h or 100 °C for 24 h

questions.chat: What BET surface area, micropore surface area and total pore volume did the best-performing composition have?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, what BET surface area, micropore surface area and total pore volume did BC-10 have?
questions.expect: SBET 496.79 m2/g, Smicro 372.99 m2/g, Vpore 0.274 cm3/g (Table 2)

questions.chat: So why did the pristine framework without biochar, with its much larger surface area, still adsorb more CO2 than that composition?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, why did the pristine framework BC-0, with its larger BET surface area, adsorb more CO2 than BC-10?
questions.expect: It did not: BC-0 adsorbed 1.16 mmol/g (26.11 cm3 STP/g), less than BC-10's 1.77 (39.59), despite its larger BET area (sec. 3.6)

questions.chat: What share of that composition's BET area is non-micropore (external) surface, and what is that share for the pristine framework?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, what share of BC-10's BET surface area is non-micropore (external) surface, and what is that share for BC-0?

questions.chat: Moving to the CO2-TPD results: what strong-site density (280-400 °C) did the best composition show, and what is reported for the pristine framework in that range?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, what CO2-TPD strong-site density (280-400 °C) did BC-10 show, and what is reported for BC-0 in that range?
questions.expect: BC-10 2.7811 mmol/g; BC-0 n.d. (not resolved) (Table 3, sec. 3.5)
questions.trap: the very strong 400-500 °C values (9.7153, 8.9706) or BC-20's 1.9227

questions.chat: Add up the weak, medium and strong site densities of the 20% composite. Does your sum match the cumulative weak-to-strong value the paper reports for it?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, add up BC-20's weak, medium and strong CO2-TPD site densities. Does the sum match the cumulative weak-to-strong value the paper reports for BC-20?
questions.expect: 1.0430 + 2.0180 + 1.9227 = 4.9837 mmol/g; yes, it matches the 4.984 mmol/g of Table 4
questions.trap: including the very strong 8.2724 (total 13.25), or using BC-10's values

questions.chat: What CO2 uptake did the activated biochar on its own show under the same conditions?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, what equilibrium CO2 uptake did the activated bamboo-derived biochar alone (A-BC) show at 298 K and about 1 bar?
questions.expect: Not given: the paper states that an A-BC CO2 isotherm is unavailable (sec. 3.6)
questions.trap: A-BC's BET area 432.10 or another sample's uptake given as A-BC's

questions.chat: Back to the adsorption isotherms: for the best composition, which model fitted better, Langmuir or Freundlich, and what R² did each give?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, which isotherm model fitted BC-10's CO2 data better, Langmuir or Freundlich, and what R² did each give for BC-10?
questions.expect: Freundlich: R² 0.8199 against Langmuir's 0.1930 (Table 5); the paper adds that neither fully captures BC-10

questions.chat: And why did the Langmuir model describe the 20% composite better than Freundlich?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, why did the Langmuir model describe BC-20's CO2 isotherm better than the Freundlich model?
questions.expect: It did not: Freundlich fitted BC-20 better (R² 0.9111 against 0.7537, lower RMSE, SSE and AICc), as for all three samples (Table 5)

questions.chat: What residual mass did the best composition and the pristine framework leave at 800 °C in the TGA under nitrogen?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, what residual mass did BC-10 and BC-0 leave at 800 °C in the TGA under nitrogen?
questions.expect: BC-10 about 47 wt%, BC-0 about 30 wt% (sec. 3.4)
questions.trap: A-BC's 79 wt% or BC-20's 43 wt%, or BC-0's 25 wt% loss below 120 °C

questions.chat: Going back to the uptakes from the start of our conversation: by what percentage does the best composition's uptake exceed the 20% composite's?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, by what percentage does BC-10's equilibrium CO2 uptake at 298 K and 1 bar exceed BC-20's?

questions.chat: In the paper's comparison with other MOF/biochar adsorbents, which reported adsorbent has the highest CO2 uptake, and which isotherm model was used for it?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, which adsorbent in the paper's comparison table of MOF/biochar CO2 adsorbents has the highest CO2 uptake, and with which isotherm model?
questions.expect: CoNi-MOF-74/biochar, 7.55 mmol/g at 298 K / 1 bar, Hill model (Table 6)

questions.chat: Finally, over how many adsorption-desorption cycles did the best composition keep its capacity?
questions.solo: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, over how many adsorption-desorption cycles did BC-10 keep its CO2 capacity?
questions.expect: Not measured: the paper says its measurements do not establish cyclic adsorption-desorption durability, and that cycling tests would be needed (secs. 1, 3.4)
